summary: Phase-2 testing for SOLEKICKS PK (Returns, Refunds+Store-Credit, Advance-Payment-on-COD, Image Upload, WhatsApp). Backend: 13/13 pytest tests PASSED in /app/backend/tests/test_phase2.py covering advance rule (>=20000 threshold, 10% advance, partially_paid), return-request + admin approval + duplicate rejection, refund STORE_CREDIT increments user balance, BANK_TRANSFER requires external_ref, over-refundable & unpaid-COD refunds rejected, PAYFAST_ORIGINAL mocked ok, store-credit redemption at checkout with REDEEMED_ON_ORDER ledger, notifications logged for ORDER_PLACED/STATUS_UPDATE/REFUND, admin /upload -> /api/files/{path} round-trip served correctly, upload requires admin auth. Frontend: guest checkout with qty 3 of AJ-4 Shadow Grail (subtotal 33750) shows checkout-advance-notice with 'Pay Rs. 3,375 Advance', order created (PK-SNK-82223) with payment_status=partially_paid, order-confirmation shows advance breakdown + green Get-WhatsApp-Updates button (wa.me link). Admin login -> Returns tab shows 4 requests + Approve works and returns become approved; Refunds tab renders; CMS tab exposes admin-hero-title/upload/save; Products -> Add Product modal exposes admin-product-image-upload; Orders rows expose admin-refund-btn + WhatsApp icon and the RefundModal auto-fills advance-paid amount (3375) with STORE_CREDIT default for COD.
critical_code_review_comments: Uploads are not garbage-collected: deleting a product or hero slide leaves the underlying object in Emergent object storage; add cleanup or a reference-counting sweep.
/api/files/{path:path} is unauthenticated so every uploaded object is public; fine for product/hero images but risky if reused for private assets later.

RefundModal always POSTs external_ref (null when empty); server accepts, but BANK_TRANSFER UI should mark the ref as required in-field. Currently server rejects with 400 which surfaces as a toast — acceptable but UX would benefit from client-side required attribute.

advance_amount is computed with Math.round on the client vs Python round(..., 2) on the server — for prices ending in .5 the client display may differ from the server by 1 rupee. Consider Math.round((subtotal*pct)/100 * 100)/100 or format via fmt.
server.py is now ~1200 lines including refunds/returns/store-credit/uploads; still would benefit from module split (returns.py, refunds.py, uploads.py).
moderate_return does not check that the current return is still 'pending' before flipping to approved/rejected — an admin can re-approve an already-refunded return; add state guard.

create_refund cascades order.status='returned' when return_request_id is provided regardless of refund method or amount — a partial refund tied to a return will mark the order returned; consider requiring full refunded_total>=paid.
Frontend `useCredit` toggle only appears when credit>0 but there is no upper-bound UI for how much to apply; the entire balance is always used. Consider allowing a partial amount input.
